original.title: Two-owner MEX response has an exact carrier normal form
assumptions: Arbitrary finite journals A,B and incoming set S over the nonnegative integers.
Two ordered MEX emissions; this is an algebraic interface statement.

exactAuditedStatement: For arbitrary finite A, B, S subset N0, u=mex(A union S), v=mex(B union S union{u}). With I=A intersect B and E(x, y)=[x notin A, y not inB]or[x in A minus B, y notin A], sorted outputs x<y satisfy x=mex(S union I), y=min{t>x:t notinS, E(x, t)}. Equality of E is exactly equality of carrier response in all finite contexts.
hypotheses: Zero-based MEX; finite journal/context sets; outputs distinct.
independentDerivationAndChecks: Every label below x is either in S or banned by both owners. If x notin A, first owner takes x; the second takes first later label outside B union S. If x in A, then x notin B and first owner takes first later label outside A union S; second take x. These are exactly the two clauses of E.
Finite bans ensure existence of y. The description is also lexicographically first edge outsideS. Therefore equal E implies equal responses.

Conversely if E and E prime differ at(x, y), choose S={0,..., y}minus{x, y}. The pair accepting the edge emits exactly{x, y}; the other cannot emit this pair by the already proved normal form. Thus responses differ. E recovers I because x notin I iff E(x, z) for all sufficiently large z, so no additional hidden coordinate is needed.
This concerns current carrier response only. It does not claim private journal updates agree or canonical state compression.
